quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When weather, road, and traffic conditions are poor, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Poor driving conditions require more space between your vehicle and others. Keep at least four seconds of distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the one you were just in.

questions.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green signs warn you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn of pedestrians, bicycles, and school zones. Drive slowly and watch for children near these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Turn left knowing that oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must wait for them and pedestrians to pass first.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates?

options.text: Cross immediately and as fast as possible.
Be ready to stop for any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop for any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to stop for trains at any railroad crossing. Wait until your entire vehicle can safely cross before moving forward. Do not shift gears while crossing.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead and a road joins from the right.

questions.question: In winter, what happens to shaded areas on roads?

options.text: They freeze at the same time as the rest of the road.
They freeze after the rest of the road.
They freeze before the rest of the road.
They thaw before the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before the rest of the road.
questions.explanation: In winter, shaded areas freeze before the rest of the road and stay icy longer. Be extra careful in these areas.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the ramp.
Slow down after you enter the ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the ramp.
Pass slower vehicles on the ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the ramp.
questions.explanation: Wait until you are on the exit ramp before you slow down. Do not slow down before entering it.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
If you plan to turn left soon.
Right away, as soon as you pass the car.
You can stay in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when there is enough distance between you and the vehicle you just passed.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs warn you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mean you are near a school. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Use turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when needed.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text confirming it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines. You may:

options.text: Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles, but only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross these lines under no circumstances.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you may not park farther than ____ inches from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, stay 18 inches or closer to the curb. Park where drivers coming from both directions can see you.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that provide directional and mileage information to drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They help you navigate unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, or bad weather.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, turn the wheel in the direction you want the car to go. When the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: To avoid becoming a dangerous and aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Speed only when there are no police officers nearby.
Make eye contact with surrounding aggressive drivers.
Tailgate to inform other drivers that you need to get somewhere.
Allow plenty of time for trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow plenty of time for trips.
questions.explanation: Bad drivers are dangerous to everyone on the road. Plan extra time for your trips so you won't feel rushed. Starting early means you won't need to break traffic rules to arrive on time.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow them are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. If you don't follow them, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.
Set grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system releases dangerous fumes. These fumes can make you very tired and drowsy while driving. They can even be deadly.

questions.question: In winter weather, overpasses and bridges:

options.text: Are affected in the same way as other roadways.
Freeze after the rest of the roads.
Freeze before the rest of the roads.
Thaw out before the rest of the roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before the rest of the roads.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before regular roads and stay icy longer. Drive slowly and carefully on these areas in freezing weather.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic lights or stop signs, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. Slow down, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again to avoid a crash.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They tell you what you must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing, no turning, and other driving rules.

questions.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions down the middle of the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is ahead. Watch for trains.

questions.question: If you are in a turn lane but want to drive straight ahead, you should:

options.text: Reverse your vehicle and merge back into traffic.
Put on your turn signal and wait to merge back into through-traffic.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the turn anyway.
questions.explanation: If you are in a turn lane, you must turn. Other drivers expect you to turn. Make the turn and then go around the block to get back to where you want to go.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:
questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: It takes longer to stop on wet or icy roads. Stopping distance also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: When following an emergency vehicle, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Stay at least four seconds behind an emergency vehicle. They need extra space to move and stop.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Only know generally where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar area. Do not start with only a vague idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down entering the curve. Speed up exiting the curve.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up entering the curve. Slow down exiting the curve.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down entering the curve. Speed up exiting the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
You cannot turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: You may ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black lettering.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn warning signs often show an advisory speed sign. This recommends a safe driving speed for the curves and turns. Never exceed the recommended speed in rain, snow, or ice, even if you feel comfortable at higher speeds in good weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must and must not do. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the roadside, what should you do?

options.text: Expect the driver may open the car door as you pass.
Expect the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver may open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, be ready for the driver to open the door. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right to escape. Steering left is dangerous—the other driver may correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces impact.

questions.question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning.
questions.explanation: Broken lines may be crossed, but solid lines generally cannot. Solid yellow lines may only be crossed when you are making a turn.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, move as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Yield to the emergency vehicle from any direction if it is using lights and/or sirens.
